rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE REGISTER OF DEEDS OF THE PROVINCE OF COMPOSTELA VALLEY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-30

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING TWO (2) ADDITIONAL TRIAL COURT BRANCHES IN COMPOSTELA VALLEY PROVINCE TO BE LOCATED IN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF COMPOSTELA AND MABINI, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION FOURTEEN (14) OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 129 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE JUDICIARY REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1980
rows.title_short: Creating Two (2) Additional Trial Court Branches in Compostela Valley to be Located in Compostela and Mabini
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-03-11, transmitted to on 2003-03-12 and received by the Senate on 2003-03-17

second_reading.remarks: The Body considered the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the           sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL OFFICIAL NONWORKING DAYS TO FALL EITHER ON A MONDAY OR A FRIDAY
rows.abstract: All official non-working days except New Year's Day, Christmas Day and Independence Day shall be scheduled to fall either on a Monday or a Friday.  The term "official non-working days" as used in this Act shall include those days duly declared and recognized by the government of the Republic of the Philippines wherein employees of both the public and private sectors are privileged not to attend work because of a national, international or traditional observance or celebration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE DRUG ENFORCEMENT ADMINISTRATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND ABOLISHING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS BOARD CREATED UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 1972' FOR THIS PURPOSE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Creation and Mission of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Administration. - An agency is hereby created to be known as the Philippine Drug Enforcement Administration (PDEA), hereinafter referred to as "PDEA", which shall provide the national policy and program direction on drug control and shall be responsible for the efficient and effective enforcement of all laws on prohibited and regulated drugs and other controlled substances.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2001-07-30

first_reading.comm_act: change of cttee. ref'l from Gov't Reorg. as per J.5; p.30(July 31,2001);a s per J. 35; p.41

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 340, AS AMENDED, WHICH ESTABLISHED A UNIFORM RETIREMENT SYSTEM FOR THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Section 3 of this Act provides for the payment of benefits to survivors of retired military personnel but it specifically excludes from entitlement to such benefits the widow of a retired officer or enlisted man if her marriage to the officer or enlisted man was contracted after his retirement from the military service.  This provision is unfair to widows who married their husbands when these men were already advanced in years and therefore needed more companionship, care and attention.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-30

rows.author: B001
rows.title_full: THE MAGNA CARTA FOR OLDER PERSONS
rows.abstract: In keeping with the constitutional mandate and addressing the needs of the elderly, this proposed bill seeks to formulate a national comprehensive plan and delineate the socio-economic and political rights of older persons, which emphasizes their empowerment, dignity, self-reliance, care, rehabilitation and productivity aging.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05987

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PHILIPPINE MARITIME AND OCEANS POLICY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Philippine Oceans Act of 2000." Rationale: The body of work and knowledge on both the social and natural dimensions of the ocean and marine structure has much more room for improvement. There is an urgent need to collect new data, update existing information, and analyze these with a perspective that is relevant to the country's interests and aspirations concerning the oceans.  There is also an urgent need to consider the world environment as well. Globalization and modern technology threatenthe oceans and seas.  We must stand guard.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATIONS OF MUTUAL FUNDS AND OTHER INVESTMENT COMPANIES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Investment Company Act of 2000." The purpose of this Act is to establish a comprehensive scheme of regulation to permit investment companies to serve their role in the capital formation process, and at the same time promote the application of fiduciary principles in the management and supervision of mutual funds and high standards of professionalism by their distributors and others who provide services to them and seek to prevent abuses and protect the interests of the public who are investorsin such companies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C136
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT TO ADDRESS THE NATIONAL WATER CRISIS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The current institutional set-up coupled with lack of resources and authority also contributed to the ineffectivity and inefficiency of water resource management. Fragmented responsibilitie s and lack of a comprehensive planning and control of water resources use and conservation need to be addressed immediately, lest we lose what has remained of our precious water resources.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C136
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE NATIONAL LAND USE POLICY AND PLANNING FRAMEWORK AND THE IMPLEMENTING MECHANISM THEREFOR, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL LAND USE ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks, primarily, to propose the enactment of a unified national land use policy that will address the issues relative to the allocation and utilization of land and other physical resources.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06056

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per J.37; p.19m

rows.author: C136
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-29, transmitted to on 2002-12-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-12-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST RESOURCES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Sustainable management means the ability to meet the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. This is the framework under which the present bill has been crafted.  Thebill aims to mark on the ground permanent boundaries for all forest lands as mandated by the 1987 constitution, in order to, among others, to accelerate and sustain the rehabilitation and protection of denuded forest areas, with watersheds as priority.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05162

rows.author: C136
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE SIQUIJOR PROVINCIAL HIGH SCHOOL IN CAIPILAN, SIQUIJOR, SIQUIJOR INTO A NATIONAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL TO BE KNOWN AS THE SIQUIJOR NATIONAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE
rows.title_short: Establishing the Siquijor National Science High School in Caipilan, Siquijor
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-03-13, transmitted to on 2002-03-18 and received by the Senate on 2002-03-18

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C136
rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE MUNICIPALITY OF ENRIQUE VILLANUEVA IN THE PROVINCE OF SIQUIJOR INTO THE MUNICIPALITY OF TALINGTING
rows.title_short: Renaming the Municipality of Enrique Villanueva into the Municipality of Talingting
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-03, transmitted to on 2004-02-05 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved the insertion of the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks; approved the amendments as contained in the C.R., if any

rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE(5)-YEAR WARRANTY PERIOD FOR GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE CONTRACTS, AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1594 `PRESCRIBING POLICIES, GUIDELINES, RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE CONTRACTS', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The contractor shall assume full responsibility for the contract work FROM THE TIME PROJECT CONSTRUCTION COMMENCED until FIVE (5) YEARS FROM its final acceptance by the Government and shall be held responsible for any damage or destruction of worksexcept those occasioned by force majeure. Except likewise for force majeure, the contractor shall be fully responsible for the safety, protection, security, and convenience of his personnel, third parties, and the public at large, as well as the works, equipment, installation and the like to be affected by his contraction work.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE GUINOBATAN-JOVE LLAR-DONSOL PROVINCIAL ROAD OF THE THIRD DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF ALBAY, INTO A NATIONAL ROAD, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Converting the Guinobatan-Jovellar-Donsol Road in Albay into a National Road
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-20, transmitted to on 2002-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2002-11-27

second_reading.remarks: Considered the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE MATACON-MAIPON- SAN RAFAEL PROVINCIAL ROAD OF THE THIRD DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF ALBAY, INTO A NATIONAL ROAD AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Converting the Matacon-Maipon San Rafael Road in Albay into a National Road
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-20, transmitted to on 2002-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2002-11-27

second_reading.remarks: Considered the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE POLANGUI-LIDONG -BUHI PROVINCIAL ROAD OF THE THIRD DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF ALBAY, INTO A NATIONAL ROAD AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Converting the Polangui-Lidong-Buhi Road in Alban into a National Road
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-20, transmitted to on 2002-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2002-11-27

second_reading.remarks: Considered the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTE POLICIES TO ELIMINATE THE TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS ESPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS, ESTABLISHING THE NECESSARY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION AND SUPPORT OF TRAFFICKED PERSONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Trafficki ng Act of 2001." Rationale: The growing feminization of poverty and migration, along with the opening of borders as an imperative of globalization, has aggravated the odious global phenomenon of labor trafficking, more particularly in women and minors. Trafficking in persons is an oppressive trade that is dehumanizing even as it exploits female and child migrants.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04432

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTOMATICALLY INCLUDING RETIRED SCHOOL TEACHERS TO BENEFIT FROM SALARY INCREASES GRANTED TO IN-SERVE TEACHERS, EFFECTING CORRESPONDING ADJUSTMENTS IN THEIR RETIREMENT PENSION
rows.abstract: "Retired Public School Teachers' Special Bonus Act of 2001." Rationale: One sector of society, however, that has been left to make do with their diminutive income are the retired public and private school teachers. After devoting their prime years and talents to the education of the nation's children and future leaders, these poor teachers retired from service, many of them with much regret. They have given the best years of their lives to service for an educated citizenry that would take overthe various aspects of national life.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS FREE OF CHARGE X-RAY AND OTHER FORMS OF LABORATORY EXAMINATIONS IN ANY GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE HOSPITALS DURING THEIR REQUIRED ANNUAL PHYSICAL EXAMINATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: X-ray and other forms of laboratory examinations shall be granted to all public school teachers in any government and private hospitals; Provided, however,  That such privilege shall only be available during the required annual physical examinationschedule.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TOTALLY BANNING LOGGING OPERATIONS FOR THE NEXT TWENTY-FIVE (25) YEARS
rows.abstract: It is hereby declared a Policy of the State to prohibit logging operations of any kind in any forest, timber land, forest reserve or watershed for the next twenty-five (25) years. It shall be unlawful for any person to cut, fell or destroy any treestanding on any forest, timber land, forest reserve or watershed within the next twenty-five (25) years from the approval of this Act. This prohibition shall not apply to trees grown in legitimate commercial tree farms.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING BLOOD BANK INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS OR HEALTH FACILITIES TO CONDUCT PRELIMINARY BLOOD EXAMINATIONS ON ALL BLOOD DONORS PRIOR TO THE ACT OF DONATION, PRESCRIBING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: It is hereby declared the policy of the State to regulate the donations of blood, both government and privately-owned commercial blood banks, hospitals or health facilities, and promote the safe method of such acts of donation for the purpose of advancing good and secure health for the nation. Toward this end, the State shall encourage widest participation among concerned government and non-government instrumentaliti es and agencies in the mobilization of a well-informed citizenry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXPEDITE THE ARRESTS OF SUSPECTED CRIMINALS BY AUTHORIZING ELECTED BARANGAY OFFICIALS TO EXECUTE AND TO AID IN THE EXECUTION OF WARRANTS OF ARREST AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Barangay Officials' Police Power Act of 2001." Any provision of law to the contrary notwithstanding , all duly elected barangay officials are hereby authorized to: (a) execute and/or severe warrants of arrest; (2) assist and coordinate with law enforcement agencies and officers in the execution and service of warrants of arrest, issued by the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, Sandiganbayan, Regional Trial Courts, Metropolitan Trial Courts, and Metropolitan Circuit Courts in the manner providedhereinafter and within their respective territorial jurisdictions without prejudice to the execution amd service of such warrants of arrest by all other law enforcement agencies and officers: Provided, That the duly elected officials of the Sangguniaang Kabataan are exempted from such mandate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING CIGARETTE/CIGAR SMOKING IN CERTAIN PUBLIC PLACES AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Anti-Smoking Act of 2001." It is hereby declared a policy of the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. It is also the policy of the State to safeguard public health by discouraging cigarette/cigar smoking which has been determined to be harmful to the health of smokers and nonsmokers alike.  To this end, the State shall regulate cigarette/cigar smoking.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Health as per J. 67; p.30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND NINE HUNDRED SIXTEEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE ACT OF 1995, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill imposes an obligation on the part of the Philippine Economic Zone (PEZA), the government agency designated to manage the development of ecozones, in regard to paying due and proper disturbance compensation to any person or group of personswho are evicted in the area where the ecozones are established. This bill also requires the appointment of qualified persons to head the PEZA Board, shifting from the old practice of just appointing somebody even those without any professional background and moral ascendancy in connection with the job of the office. This is necessary in order to really professionalize the performance of the authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING VACATION AND SICK LEAVE BENEFITS OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any provision of existing law to the contrary notwithstanding , an employee, whether permanent or temporary, of the National Government, its branches, agencies and instrumentaliti es, including local governments, and of government-owne d and/or controlled corporations and their subsidiaries, shall be entitled to thirty (30) days vacation leave and thirty (30) days sick leave with full pay, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays, for each calendar year of service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING FISH CULTURE PENS IN LAKES THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: The construction and maintenance of fish pens in lakes and tributaries thereof throughout the country is prohibited. For purposes of this Act, fish culture pens shall mean any enclosure wherein aquatic animals are grown in a prepared medium. Violation of this Act shall be punished by imprisonment of no less than one (1) year nor more than five (5) years and a fine of not less than Ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) nor more than One hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00) at the discretion of the Court.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED PERSONS FROM HAVING ACCESS TO FIREARMS
rows.abstract: "Firearms Access Prevention Act."  This proposed measure seeks to impose a ban on unauthorized persons from having access to firearms. In this Act, punishable acts related to unauthorized access to firearms and the indiscriminate use of them are also defined and imposed the penalties of both imprisonment and a fine of not more than one hundred thousand pesos.  This stiff penalty to such violation is conceived to institutionaliz e a deterrence in the furtherance of the commission of crimes related to what is prohibited in this Act.  To further institutionaliz e a system of safekeeping of firearms a secure gun storage or safety device is urged to be used by firearms owners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN THE EXISTING MECHANISM FOR DETERRENCE TO THE COMMISSION OF CRIME IN THE CONDUCT OF FRATERNITY, SORORITY AND OTHER CONFRATERNITY INITIATION RITES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHT THOUSAND AND FORTY-NINE
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 8049, otherwise known as the Anti-Hazing Law in order to further strengthen the existing mechanism for deterrence to the commission of crime in the conduct of fraternity, sorority, and confraternity initiation rites.  Hence, senseless violence or death is averted.  With the new provisions added in the existing Republic Act No. 8049, therefore, it is hoped that a stronger deterrence to the commission of hazing, thereby causing unwanted casualties and deaths of young and vibrant people, in the process of initiation rites is established.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL TELEPHONE COMPANIES TO INSTALL A HOT LINE SYSTEM FOR THE USE OF LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES AND FIRE STATIONS IN THE EVENT OF EMERGENCY AND CALAMITY
rows.abstract: All telephone companies are hereby required to install a hot line system consisting of alarm systems and other warning devices to ensure the availability of efficient communication system for the use and prompt response of law enforcement agencies and fire stations in the event of emergency and calamity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL INSURANCE BENEFITS TO ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PAYMENT OF ITS PREMIUMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In addition to the insurance benefits given to teachers by the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) under Republic Act No. 8291 a term insurance coverage to all public school teachers providing the following benefits shall be granted: (a)  death benefits of two hundred thousand pesos (P200,000.00) to all teachers who are in active service; (b) burial expenses of fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00) to all teachers who are in active service; and (c) reimbursement of actual medical expenses ofall teachers, whether retired or in the active service, but not to exceed one hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING SMOKING IN PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION AND BUILDINGS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Smoking is strictly prohibited in public transportation and buildings. For purposes of this Act, smoking shall include cigars and cigarette smoking and pipe smoking or any device creating cigarette or tobacco fumes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Health as per J. 67; p.30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENTS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Sec. 284. Allotment of Internal Revenue Taxes. - Local government units shall have a share in the national revenue taxes based on the collection of the third fiscal year preceding the current fiscal year as follows:  (a) On the first year of the effectivity of this Code, thirty percent (30%); (b) On the second year, thirty-five percent (35%); [and] (c) On the third UNTIL THE EIGHTH year [and thereafter], forty percent (40%); (D) ON THE NINTH YEAR, FORTY-FIVE PERCENT (45%); (E) ON THE TENTH YEAR, FIFTY PERCENT (50%); (F) ON THE ELEVENTH YEAR, FIFTY-FIVE PERCENT (55%); (G) ON THE TWELFTH YEAR AND THEREAFTER (60%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ABOLISH THE PROVISION OF AUTOMATIC TERMINATION OF SUBSEQUENT MARRIAGE BY THE RECORDING OF THE AFFIDAVIT OF REAPPEARANCE OF THE ABSENT SPOUSE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 42 OF THE FAMILY CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Article 42 of the said Code which provides for an automatic termination of subsequent marriage "by the recording of the affidavit of reappearance of the absent spouse," however, appears to be in congruent with the spirit to which the Family Code of the Philippines was conceived. So that while it adheres to the contemporary trends and conditions, the specific provision in Article 42 of the Code does not simply manifest so, for it denies the right of the contracted party to exercise his/her optional prerogative to which marriage he/she feels more duty bound considering his/her existing condition. The proposed bill justly gives the contracted party, given the former acted in good faith, the legal right to exercise an optional preroogative in his/her current marriage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIX HUNDRED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MARINE POLLUTION DECREE OF 1974
rows.abstract: The proposed measure defines the guidelines under which the commandant of the Philippine Coast Guard may allow the dumping of waste materials. This likewise authorizes the adoption of a dumping system which shall take into account the chemical composition and attributes of waste materials so to avoid pollution in our waters.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIX THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED SEVENTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE GENERICS ACT OF 1988, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill therefore seeks to amend Republic Act 6675 which is aimed at ensuring stronger deterrence against dubious profit-oriented pharmaceutical cumpanies and distributors which, like leeches, will continuously suck blood to many of the poor Filipinos.  To protect the public from these elements in the pharmaceutical industry, this proposed legislation attempts to add the following provisions: 1) definition and requirements for quality control standards; and 2) stiffer provision on quality, manufacturer's identity and responsibility. In short this bill, on one hand, intends to facilitate the protection of consumers in so far as pharmaceutical products are concerned - to protect citizens from the harmful effects of fake or substandard druggs and medicines. Thus, provision are included for quality control standard.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROHIBIT DISCRIMINATION IN THE RECRUITMENT, EMPLOYMENT, PROMOTION AND DISMISSAL OF ANY LESBIAN OR GAY IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EMPLOYMENT SOLELY ON ACCOUNT OF DIFFERENCE IN SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to prohibit any form of discrimination against lesbians and gays of the labor force especially those pertinent to their recruitment, employment, promotion and dismissal. Corresponding penalties therefor are also hereby provided to ensure a more responsible and equitable treatment of these mostly stereotyped sectors of Philippine society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A BI-ANNUAL FOGGING OPERATION NATIONWIDE, ALLOCATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Truly, while there are constitutional provisions which assure every Filipino individual for their right to health services from the government, it is still deemed necessary that specific and concrete programs and actions be designed to effect them and to make said provisions relevant and responsive to the current needs of the people.  It is in this spirit that the proposed bill is conceived.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DEVOLUTIONIZE TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT THE AUTHORITY WITH RESPECT OVER THE RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SPECIFIC PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED SIXTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: If one wants national services to grow and develop, one must not think of the present generation alone.  If we want the world to attain universal progress, unity and peace, we must work for the well-being of the children, look after their health, education, human rights, moral and spiritual values.  This bill, therefore, seeks for the creation of the Local Council for Children to be established in every city or municipality to directly oversee the children's well being and strictly monitor andprohibit child abuse.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MONTHLY ALLOWANCES FOR THE MEMBERS OF LUPONG TAGAPAMAYAPA AND THE PANGKAT NG TAGAPAGKASUNDO, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The Members of the Lupon and the Pangkat have greatly contributed to the promotion of peace, harmony and solidarity in the community even if their membership is voluntary and without compensation. The fact that the Members of the Lupon and the Pangkat have been instrumental in unclogging court dockets by settling a good number of cases referred to them in their level cannot be overemphasized. They have likewise given the government tremendous savings and, the monthly incentives that may be given to them is only just and fair.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPROVING PHILIPPINE COMMITMENT TO HUMAN RIGHTS PROMOTION AND PROTECTION BY AMENDING BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 22, ENTITLED `AN ACT PENALIZING THE MAKING OR DRAWING AND ISSUANCE OF A CHECK WITHOUT SUFFICIENT FUNDS OR CREDIT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: Despite its laudable purpose of ensuring the stability of the banking and payments system for a healthy economy, BP 22 has been much abused thereby making it anti-poor in practice. This particular law has caused untold hardship and suffering to the weaker and poorer sectors of the Filipino people as well as the clogging of the dockets of the courts of justice as to make such courts almost full-time collection agencies. BP Blg. 22 (An Act Penalizing the Making or Drawing and Issuanceof a Check Without Sufficient Funds or Credit and For Other Purposes) is hereby amended as follows: SECTION 1 - A. EXCEPTION. WHERE THE CHECK IS ISSUED AS PART OF AN ARRANGEMENT TO GUARANTEE OR SECURE THE PAYMENT OF AN OBLIGATION, WHETHER PRE-EXISTINNG OR NOT, THE DRAWER SHALL NOT BE CRIMINALLY LIABLE UNDER THIS ACT OR UNDER ARTICLE 315 (2D) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING FOR EACH REGION A FIVE (5) HECTARE ARBORETUM, DECLARING IT AS PROTECTED AREAS FOR ECOLOGICAL PRESERVATION, ALLOCATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There shall be established in each region, under the direct supervision of the Department of Environment and Natural REsources, a five (5) hectare arboretum which shall be declared as protected areas for the purpose of ecological preservation. The National Capital Region (NCR), the Autonomous Region of Muslm Mindanao (ARMM) and the Cordillera Autonomous Region (CAR) shall be included in the regions where this Act shall be implemented.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RESTRICT THE ACCESS OF YOUTH TO CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: "Contrl Youth Access to Tobacco Act." Significant provisions of this bill are: (1) VENDING MACHINES - Vending Machines may be used to sell tobacco products only in an area or establishment from which individuals under the minimum age prescribed by subsection (b) are denied access. (2) MINIMUM AGE - No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer or tobacco products may offer or distribute tobacco products may sell a tobacco product to an individual who is less than 18 years old. (3) PACKAGES OF CIGARETTES - Only cigarettes in a package of 20 cigarettes may be sold or distributed by a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer or tobacco products. (4) SAMPLING - No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer or tobacco products may offer or distribute tobbacco products for sampling except in an area or establishment from which minors are denied access.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING BLOOD BANK INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS OR HEALTH FACILITIES TO CONDUCT PRELIMINARY BLOOD EXAMINATIONS ON ALL BLOOD DONORS PRIOR TO THE ACT OF DONATION, PRESCRIBING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All government and privately-owned commercial blood banks, hospitals or health facilities shall be required to conduct thorough preliminary blood examinations on all blood donors prior to the act of donation.  Any result which indicates positive contamination of any dreaded virus or disease in blood samples of a prospective donor shall be reported immediately to proper authorities of the Department of Health (DOH).

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE MANDATORY AND PERIODIC DRUG TESTING UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Mandatory and periodic blood testing shall cover the following: (a) Applicants for marriage license. - The blood testing for applicants for marriage license shall be an additional requirement before the issuance of aforementioned license to: (1) determine the fitness of the contracting parties; (2) avoid cases of separation and annulment of marriages based on ignorance of a contracting partner due to lingering illness of the other; and(3) avoid further spread of genetic deficiencies and other diseases; and (b) Applicants for Overseas Employment. - No persons shall be issued overseas employment certificate unless he undergoes a comprehensive blood test every before departure for overseas employment and upon arrival therefrom.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ALLOCATION FOR THE SPECIAL EDUCATION FUND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Section 235, Chapter 5 of Republic Act Numbered SDeventy-one Hundred and Sixty, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" is hereby amended to read as follows: "Chapter 5. - Special Leaves on Real Property Sec. 235. Additional Levy on Real Property for the Special Education Fund (SEF).- A province or city or a municipality [within the Metropolitan Manila Area] may levy and collect an annual tax of [one] TWO percent [(1%)] (2%) on the assessed value of real property which shall be an addition to the basic real property tax. The proceeds thereof shall exclusively accrue to the Special Education Fund (SEF) IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 7 OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FIFTY-FOUR FORTY-SEVEN.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF THE MINORITY FLOOR LEADER OF THE SANGGUNIAN CONCERNED IN THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is a well known fact that the Minority in any Sanggunian represents the other side in the community. They are the fiscalizers in the disbursement of funds and promulgation of laws in the Sanggunian and their presence in the Local School Board will give added assurance that the administration of this Special fund is subjected to the scrutiny and safeguard that it deserves. Also, this will help promote the general support to programs formulated by the Board and will contribute to asound local governance.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM ANY AND ALL TAXES THE AMOUNTS AND SIMILAR BENEFITS THAT WILL BE GIVEN TO AND RECEIVED BY HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS AS COMPENSATION UNDER THE JUDGE MANUEL REAL DECISION, AND ALL THOSE SIMILARLY SITUATED
rows.abstract: Rationale: One significant accomplishment that the victims obtained in their efforts to seek justice was the decision in their favor rendered by Judge Manuel Real of the United States in a class suit litigated therein in behalf of more than nine thousand (9,000) sufferers, or their heirs, specifically mandating compensation for damages and injuries suffered. Until today, no such compensation has yet been made.  Any such compensdation is not income. At most, it will be only rehabilitative or restorative, but may in fact never approximate the depth and the magnitude of the injury or suffering.

rows.author: C061
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AS NATIONAL POLICY THE FREEDOM OF THE FILIPINO FROM ONEROUS, UNREASONABLE AND UNCONSCIONABLE DEBT OR OBLIGATION, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 31 (b) OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1177 AND SIMILAR LAWS, DECREES, EXECUTIVE AND ADMINISTRATIVE ORDERS, AND CIRCULARS
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Filipino has suffered for long, and suffered bitterly from the burdens of those debts or obligations which have eaten up as much as thirty to forty percent of the annual national budget, made conveniently and contemptibly by the automatic appropriation provision in Presidential Decree No. 1177, specifically Sections 31 (b) thereof, and similar laws, decrees, executive and administrative orders, or circulars. Section 31 (b) of Presidential Decree No. 1177 and similar laws, decrees, executive orders, administrative orders, or circulars, are hereby repealed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-30
